title: Danang International Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Edition Was Like
seo_title: Danang International Marathon 2027 Review | Da Nang
meta_description: Danang International Marathon review: nearly 9,000 runners from 75+ countries on 22 March 2026, a Filipino men's winner, and about $20,000 raised for charity.
dek: Da Nang's international marathon drew nearly 9,000 runners from more than 75 countries in March 2026. Here is what that edition was like, ahead of 2027.
verdict: The Danang International Marathon is a coastal city marathon with an international field. The 2026 edition, on 22 March, drew nearly 9,000 runners from more than 75 countries and territories [1]. The Philippines' Edsel Moral, a factory worker and one of the country's leading amateur marathoners, won the men's race in 2:30:42, and Vu Khanh Linh the women's in 3:01:20 [1]. About US$20,000 was donated to social organisations in Da Nang [1]. If you want an early-season marathon in central Vietnam with a genuinely international mix of runners, it is a good choice.

sections.heading: The 2026 Edition
paragraphs: Nearly 9,000 runners from more than 75 countries and territories took part on 22 March 2026 [1]. There were marathon, half marathon and 5 km races [1].
About US$20,000 raised through the race was donated to social organisations in the city [1].

sections.heading: The Front of the Race
paragraphs: Edsel Moral of the Philippines won the men's marathon in 2:30:42 [1]. He works in a factory, trains after work, and has won several marathons in the Philippines [1]. Vu Khanh Linh, 30, of Ho Chi Minh City, won the women's marathon in 3:01:20, three years after taking up marathon running [1].
Trieu Thi Binh won the women's half marathon in 1:22:56, and the men's 5 km was decided by less than a second [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a marathon in central Vietnam in March with a big international field.
The reporting says little about the route itself, so look at the 2027 course map before you plan your pacing.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2026 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.
